answer: Weight grows from a single tenure thread that cannot be split: each identity must finish a sequential memory-hard proof whose state builds only over epochs it personally survived, like a grove growing one ring per season. Splitting stake across clones resets every clone thread to zero, and the finished proof becomes a non-transferable relic of that identity own history - it cannot be copied, pooled, or run in parallel. Adding one more head therefore costs a full fresh tenure, not a slice of an old one.
